**NON-GOALS ADDED BY THIS REVISION** (the bullets above are carried from the predecessor plan and
every one of them still binds; these are additional):
- **`κ` IS NOT RE-DEFINED AS A SEMANTIC BISIMULATION QUOTIENT, AND NO PHASE MOVES TO AN EXACT-GAP
  COORDINATE** (Ruling 13). Bisimulation is a METHOD here — write the relation with unknown
  thresholds, list the one-step cases, solve — and never a definition. `Dmax` is a union over
  subsets of `Q × ClType φ × CK …` and `relK` an image over finite counter representatives, so the
  carrier must be ENUMERABLE and the class map COMPUTABLE; the semantic quotient supplies neither,
  and finite index is already free (`anchorCells_finite`). A dispatch that reaches for either is
  reaching for a tautology that no consumer can use.
- **NO RECORD CITES `no_transferSys_links_collisions` AS OBSTRUCTING A FINER QUOTIENT** (Ruling 13).
  It rules out a transfer system linking every collision of the FILED `kappa` at clip `3`, and
  nothing more; a transfer system can only ever link indistinguishable points, so a correctly
  derived quotient is untouched by it.
- **THE STEP-FRAGMENT RESULT IS NOT OVER-READ, AND THE BASE CASE IS NOT THE THEOREM** (Rulings 8 and
  12). `cellAt_const_of_kappa_eq_stepFrag` and its siblings cover formulas whose `untl`/`snce` sit
  at the guard `⊥` only. `thetaC` and `mixC` each use ONE JUMP and are NOT covered; no record may
  cite the fragment result as bearing on either family, as weakening the compiled refutation of the
  filed statement, or as evidence that the whole-language agreement holds at any clip.
- **THE CONJECTURED WHOLE-LANGUAGE CLIP IS NEVER RECORDED AS PROVED** (Ruling 10). `2 * (dBack φ +
  dFwd φ) + 2` is proved TIGHT on the step fragment and dominates every compiled lower bound; that
  it SUFFICES for the whole language is a conjecture and a theorem of no file. Every docstring,
  record and summary this plan writes states the two halves separately.
- **PHASE 11.37's THRESHOLD HYPOTHESES ARE NOT DISCHARGED FROM `ParamsOk` BY THIS PLAN** (Ruling
  11). `2 * (dBack + dFwd) ≤ Tc, Tn` arrive as EXPLICIT hypotheses. That they are far below `Tcof`
  is plausible and uncompiled; a phase that asserts the discharge without compiling it has
  manufactured a fact.
- **NO PHASE OF THIS PLAN EDITS `.claude/**`.** The research round's recommendation for a pattern
  note on deriving thresholds from closure conditions is a source-store edit in another repository's
  tree (`.claude/` here is a regenerated deploy artifact), and it is recorded as an open follow-up
  rather than taken.
- **ZERO DEBT, RESTATED FOR THE NEW PHASES.** No `sorry`, no `axiom`, no `native_decide`, no
  vacuous definition (`def X := True`, a `noncomputable` `Decidable`-valued declaration, or any
  other placeholder), no finite-width assumption and no finite-fibre retreat, in ANY library module,
  in ANY phase. The single carried exception is unchanged and is confined to the demoted Phase
  11.33: an outcome-(b) measured account may isolate ONE `sorry` on its one named goal INSIDE the
  evidence fixture, where it IS the measurement. Phases 11.36-11.40 carry no such exception — their
  deliverables are compiled declarations, and a phase that cannot compile one returns a measured
  account with the goal state written out and the phase marked `[BLOCKED]` or `[PARTIAL]`, never a
  placeholder.

## Risks & Mitigations

### Risks route (Q-1) adds, and their mitigations

- **The construction half may not exist at all.** Phase 21 is four objects none of which is
  written, in a tree whose only comparable construction is excluded on four counts. Nothing in this
  task shows a model satisfying `ladderConstruct`'s specification exists. **Mitigation**: the
  carrier is Phase 21's FIRST deliverable and is complete and reportable on its own; the phase is
  bounded at one dispatch for the remaining three objects and returns `[PARTIAL]` rather than
  running unbounded; and the phase's `Timing` is NOT COSTABLE with the reason stated rather than an
  hour figure invented (Ruling 24).
- **`Dmax` may not be a certified set, which would make the construction half unstatable at
  `Dmax`.** `dmax_certStabK` and `dmax_certBoxK` do not exist and the union that defines `Dmax`
  does not preserve conditions (5) and (6) (`CounterQuotient.lean:105-113`). **Mitigation**:
  `ladderConstruct` carries `certAdmK R` as an EXPLICIT hypothesis and is deliberately NOT stated
  at `Dmax`; whether to attempt `dmax_certStabK`/`dmax_certBoxK` is named as a separate finding,
  reported rather than taken.
- **Ruling 34's assignment may be wrong.** `ladderSound` and `Dmax ⊆ Real` cannot both hold as
  filed; this plan assigns the falsity to the latter on literature grounds, and the assignment is
  INFERRED from compiled objects, not itself compiled. **Mitigation**: Phase 20's FIRST task is an
  attack on the read-off containment, on `Qc`/`thetaC` and on the chain object `Qm m`/`chainC`; a
  landed separating witness is a complete, reportable outcome that falsifies the assignment and
  returns the statement question to the user rather than being repaired in place. Phase 15.2's
  exclusion record names this contingency from the phase it would overturn.
- **Three load-bearing refutations are currently unwired.** Four of this plan's exclusion records
  cite evidence that lives only in a report appendix, where CI does not reach it and where it rots
  silently. **Mitigation**: Ruling 35, Phase 19 (wave 1, no dependency, enterable immediately), and
  the standing qualifier "compiled in a report appendix, unwired" at every such citation until
  Phase 19 closes and its last task strikes them.
- **Copying four appendix blocks may fail on drift.** The appendices compiled against the tree at
  and after commit `d57d016e8`; `ladder-cell-agreement-refutation.lean` has changed since.
  **Mitigation**: Phase 19 records a non-compiling block as a DRIFT FINDING and stops, rather than
  repairing a report's mathematics; and its one import change is derived from a re-measured import
  graph rather than from either report's literal (and mutually contradictory) instruction.
- **The object-dependent clip may look like a cheap rescue and be taken untested.** It is the one
  unrefuted route and the temptation is exactly the one that cost this task four refuted
  adoptions. **Mitigation**: Ruling 31 (attack before adopt, now vindicated twice over), Ruling 36
  item 3, and Phase 22, whose own prohibitions forbid adopting it, attempting an agreement at it,
  or describing it as settled — and whose Goal is explicitly to record a question, not answer one.
- **Both added signatures are authored at plan time and NOT compiled.** This revision runs no
  build. **Mitigation**: the `(Q-1) PAIR` sub-block says so in its own first paragraph rather than
  implying a compile record it does not have; Phases 20 and 21 each diff their landed signature
  against the pin token-for-token and report any difference as a Statement Fidelity finding.

**THE (Q-1) REVISION'S FOUR ADDED PHASES, placed in the same ordering.** Phase **19** has no
dependency and sits at **wave 1** — it is enterable immediately and is the first thing any dispatch
should run, because four of this plan's exclusion records cite evidence that is compiled in a report
appendix and unwired until it closes (Ruling 35). Phase **22** depends on 19 alone and sits at
**wave 2**. Phases **20** and **21** join wave 24 as shown. **Phases 11.49, 11.40, 15.2 and 16 are
annotated EXCLUDED and keep the ordering slots they held when they were live**, exactly as the
earlier bypassed phases do: an ordering slot is not a pending obligation.

| Wave | Phases | Blocked by |
|------|--------|------------|
| 1 | **19** | -- |
| 2 | **22** | **19** |

Phases within the same wave can execute in parallel. **A wave number is a dependency ordering, not
a schedule**, and no closed phase's own recorded wave placement is altered by the re-derivation
above — the bypassed phases keep the positions they held when they were live, annotated EXCLUDED so
no reader mistakes an ordering slot for a pending obligation.

**WHAT THIS REVISION CHANGED ABOUT THE GRAPH (ROUTE (R-3) THEN (R-2)).** TWO phases were ADDED,
TWO `[PARTIAL]` headings were RELOCATED past every open phase in file order, ONE open phase was
RE-POINTED, and ONE `Depends on` was WIDENED. No wave placement of any closed phase moved, no
closed body was edited, and no marker changed anywhere. **11.48** is route (R-3) itself: the
refutation attempt at a `(K1)`-admissible modulus, on `R4` AND on `B5`, carrying decision 21's
obligation verbatim, **before any repaired relation is adopted**. **11.49** is route (R-2) and is
conditional on 11.48's outcome (b): the object half of `(K1)` as the hypothesis of
`exists_rowLinked_path`, its bridge to `ParamsOk`, the count moves over the LANDED scaffold, and
the `untl` clause — `Timing` **NOT COSTABLE** by Ruling 24, carried. **They are a SEQUENCE and
never one phase** (Ruling 27): no phase of this plan both attacks a relation and adopts it.
**11.40**'s `Depends on` moves from the `[PARTIAL]` **11.47** to **11.49**, with its `Timing`, its
three Goal items, its task list, its prohibitions, its Scope Hypothesis and its verification
carried unchanged — the FOURTH re-pointing of that phase and for the fourth time because the lemma
its first task consumes does not exist in the library. **11.44 and 11.47 keep `[PARTIAL]`, are NOT
re-entered, and are RELOCATED past Phase 18 in file order** (Ruling 28); 11.47 additionally gains a
`#### Recorded Outcome` block, and both notices now name their continuation BY RULE. ONE
`Depends on` line was WIDENED: **Phase 18's gains `11.48`**, so the final phase observes route
(R-3)'s verdict directly even on the branch where 11.49 and 11.40 close by exclusion.

**THE SELECTOR ORDER AFTER THIS REVISION, AND WHY THE HAZARD IS NOW CLOSED STRUCTURALLY.** The
orchestrator's phase selector takes the first heading in FILE ORDER whose marker parses as open; it
cannot read a ruling and it cannot check whether a phase's declared input exists. Under the
predecessor plan both `[PARTIAL]` headings stood EARLIER in file order than everything that
continues them, so 11.44 was captured on every cycle and 11.47 would have been captured next —
and the (O-1) revision's repair, a notice redirecting by the explicit number `11.46`, **went stale
the moment 11.46 closed**, costing two hand-redirected dispatches. **This revision moves both
`[PARTIAL]` headings past Phase 18** and **re-words every RE-ENTRY NOTICE to name its continuation
by the RULE "the first open phase at or after 11.48 in file order"**, which is evaluated against
the live file and cannot go stale (Ruling 28). After this revision the first open heading in file
order is **11.48**, and the intended order is 11.48, 11.49, 11.40, 12.2, 13, 14, 15.1, 15.2, 16,
17, then 11.30 and 11.31, then 18 — every one of those selections has its own `Depends on`
satisfied by the time it is reached. **Numerically out-of-order file position carries no meaning in
this plan**: 11.23 through 11.27 already precede 11.22 and 11.21, and 11.41-11.49 already precede
11.40.

**THE ONE ENTERABLE PHASE OF THIS PLAN IS 11.48, AND THERE IS ONLY ONE.** Phase 11.49 becomes
enterable the moment 11.48 closes on outcome (b), and 11.40 after that; the three are a SEQUENCE,
not a wave, because each consumes the previous one's compiled object.

### Phase 11.2: The Pin Cascade, Front Half — Regime Exhaustiveness, Finiteness, and the Sizing [COMPLETED]

**ENTERABLE NOW, AND GATED ON NOTHING OPEN.** Re-confirmed at this revision's authoring rather than
carried: its two prerequisites (Phases 7 and 11) are both closed; `exists_spliced_ladderPath`,
`exists_spliced_ladderPath_of_pend_past`, `pinCompat_of_ladderPath`, `pend_past_of_nxtAt_lt`,
`clipIdx_regime_of_eq`, `nxtAt_lipschitz`, `nxtAt_lipschitz_two_sided` and
`cntAt_le_nxtAt_succ_of_idle_past` are all present in `LadderAgree.lean`; and
`exists_spliced_ladderPath_of_idle_past` — Phase 11.8's deliverable — is present nowhere, so this
pair's work is genuinely unlanded. Nothing the abandoned round or the live successor chain landed
changes any of that, because all of it sits ABOVE this module in the import DAG (finding 9).

**Goal**: Land, as named exported lemmas in `LadderAgree.lean`, the three facts the cascade
construction needs before it can be written, none of which requires the construction itself: (1)
REGIME EXHAUSTIVENESS — `pend_past_of_nxtAt_lt` is the dichotomy and `clipIdx_regime_of_eq` says a
class collision at a fixed next deadline stays inside one regime, so the landed
`exists_spliced_ladderPath_of_pend_past` and the cascade together cover every collision the lift
must transport, with no path ever carried from one regime into the other; (2) FINITENESS — the set
of pinned regions between an idle position `p ≤ a` on the original path and the splice point `a` is
finite, PROVED from `p` being idle rather than assumed, which is what makes the cascade's iteration
well-founded; (3) the SIZING, stated as a COUNT. No new path and no construction is built here.

**Why this phase exists, and why it is not optional**: `pinCompat_of_ladderPath` (compiled, Phase
11) proves that the region-start countdowns of EVERY ladder path are pairwise
`1`-Lipschitz-compatible, because a region start's countdown IS the deadline register's value at
the idle position before it (`cntAt_eq_nxtAt_of_idle_pend`) and the register is `1`-Lipschitz
(`nxtAt_lipschitz_two_sided`). Lengthening one region by `l` raises that one pin by `l` and moves no
earlier region start, so compatibility must be re-established rather than assumed. The condition is
forced by the carrier, not an artefact of the lift lemma's shape.

**Tasks**:

      that finiteness FROM `p` being idle rather than assuming it — that derivation is the content
      of this item, and it is what makes the cascade's iteration well-founded.

**And deciding the schema decides this plan's own filed statements.** `CellLEZeroConstOfKappaEq` is the
instance `t := z` of `cellAt_const_of_kappa_eq`'s recorded signature with one additional hypothesis
(the closure carries no `⊡` letter), so the recorded statement IMPLIES the schema; and
`ladderRealized`'s right-hand side depends on `(c, n)` only through `kappa Tc Tn P B (c, n)`, so it
assigns `kappa`-colliding states the same cell and implies the schema too. A refutation of the schema
under `ParamsOk` therefore refutes BOTH filed statements outright. That implication is derived here, at
plan time, precisely so that no implement dispatch has to derive it mid-proof or guess what a
refutation licenses.

**The statement this phase commits to, in full.** Recorded here token-for-token so that a later
dispatch lands it without a Statement-Fidelity question, and deliberately NOT added to the
`## Lean Challenge Statements` block: that block's identifier set must equal the `- **Goals**:` set,
whose members are this task's six FILED theorems, and a probe declaration is not a filed Goal — the
forty-fifth, forty-sixth and forty-seventh wired probes set that precedent. The probe declares, in
namespace `Probe761T`, the tight doubling chain re-declared verbatim from the archived prototypes (a
standalone file under `specs/**` is not on the Lake library path, so it cannot be imported and must be
re-declared, exactly as the successor task's own two prototypes did), and then:

```lean
-- In namespace Probe761T, over the chain `tightChain` and the parameter outputs of the
-- periodicity fixpoint, with `chi` the separating stab-free closure formula:

theorem tightChain_deletion_derivative_not_ladderPath
    (m l : Nat) (hl : 0 < l) (hdvd : l ∣ Pof step pend lab chi + 1)
    (z : Int) (hz : Tcof step pend lab chi ≤ cntAt tightChain z) :
    ¬ IsLadderPath step pend (delIterWalk tightChain z m l) := sorry

theorem cellLEZeroConstOfKappaEq_refuted :
    ¬ CellLEZeroConstOfKappaEq step pend fwd bwd lab chi
        (Tcof step pend lab chi) (Tnof step pend lab chi)
        (Pof step pend lab chi) (Bof step pend lab chi) := sorry

theorem exists_refuting_tight_collision :
    ParamsOk step pend lab chi (Tcof step pend lab chi) (Tnof step pend lab chi)
        (Pof step pend lab chi) (Bof step pend lab chi)
      ∧ (∀ psi : PlusFormula, PlusFormula.stab psi ∉ plusSubformulaClosure chi)
      ∧ (∃ q c n c' n' : _, kappa (Tcof step pend lab chi) (Tnof step pend lab chi)
            (Pof step pend lab chi) (Bof step pend lab chi) (c, n)
          = kappa (Tcof step pend lab chi) (Tnof step pend lab chi)
            (Pof step pend lab chi) (Bof step pend lab chi) (c', n')
          ∧ c ≠ c' ∧ c ∈ Adm pend q ∧ c' ∈ Adm pend q)
      ∧ ¬ CellLEZeroConstOfKappaEq step pend fwd bwd lab chi
            (Tcof step pend lab chi) (Tnof step pend lab chi)
            (Pof step pend lab chi) (Bof step pend lab chi) := sorry
```

no certificate object enters the argument.

**The sub-claim that resisted, stated exactly.** Going from non-liftability of the chain's
deletion-derivatives to `¬ CellLEZeroConstOfKappaEq` needs the realized-type layer over the chain,
and the missing link is NOT an arithmetic one. A cell equality at a `kappa`-collision `(c, n)`
versus `(c', n')` with `c' < c` asks that every type realized at the first state be realized at the
second by SOME ladder path through it. Nothing makes that path a deletion-derivative of the chain:
the cell quantifies over every history through the state, so non-liftability of the derivatives
does not by itself exclude the equality. What is owed is a closure formula whose own letters FORCE
the realizing path to be a deletion-derivative of the chain — and the two compiled facts that bear
on the choice both cut against the obvious candidates: the schema is refuted at the frozen
`ParamsOkPre` whose `(K4)` reads the backward depth alone, while under `ParamsOk` the same probe's
`not_paramsOkK4_two` and `kappa_D_dissolves` show the two-depth predicate rejects that clip and
dissolves that collision. A formula at `atom`-level depth is no use either: the closure of
`chiT := atom p` has a single member, so its cell depends on the object state alone and the schema
holds for it. The owed object is therefore a deeper formula together with a surviving collision,
which is the open core itself.

**Three statement-level findings, reported and not worked around.**

1. **The recorded statement is false at `m = 0`.** It quantifies `(m l : Nat)` with `0 < l` and no
   constraint on `m`; at `m = 0` the deletion-derivative deletes nothing and IS the chain, which is
   a ladder path. It needs `0 < m`. The landed theorems carry `hm : 0 < m` and honest names of
   their own; the recorded block is left exactly as recorded.
2. **The recorded conclusion is register-specific, and the record's claim is not.**
   `¬ IsLadderPath step pend (delIterWalk …)` constrains the deleted walk's own register, so it is
   weaker than "the derivative does not LIFT". The landed form quantifies the countdown and the
   register away, which is the claim the README makes and the claim a consumer needs.
3. **The object must be the chain with pins unbounded above.** On the archived prototype's
   finite-`J` chain the LAST region is followed by the idle-forever tail and so carries no pin
   above it; deleting a block from it moves no later pin, the register demand at the last pin drops
   by the deleted amount while every earlier pin keeps its own, and the `1`-Lipschitz pin condition
   admits that. A finite-`J` chain therefore HAS a lifting deletion-derivative and the claim is
   false at that object. The probe declares the unbounded chain and says so in its own docstring;
   the archived finite-`J` prototype is unmodified and is not restated.

### Phase 11.11: The Idle-Insertion Walk, Its Primitive, and Its Four Local Ladder Conditions [COMPLETED]

**GATED ON PHASE 11.10's VERDICT, AND CARRIES NO OPEN MATHEMATICS OF ITS OWN.** The first missing
component the Phase 11.8 handoff names — "no declaration anywhere builds an idle-insertion walk" —
is a DEFINITION, and a definition together with its elementary local facts is landable whether or
not the pin half ever closes. This phase lands exactly that, plus ONE recorded decision, and no
existential.

**Goal**: Define the inserted walk over the spliced one and land the four LOCAL hypotheses
`exists_ladderPath_of_walk` consumes — `hw`, `hidle`, `hpp`, `hpi` (finding 27) — together with the
two pointwise facts at and above the insertion site that make `objAt g' v = objAt g v` and
`cntAt g' v = cntAt g v + l` hold BY CONSTRUCTION at the comparison position rather than by a
further argument. **No pin hypothesis is touched**: `hpins` and `hn₀` are Phase 11.12's whole
content.

**The shape, as a PLAN-TIME PROPOSAL whose local conditions this phase's own verification
measures — not as a construction known to work.** The index map pushes the past below the
insertion site `u` down by `d` and lengthens the idle run at `u` downward by `d`, leaving every
position above `u` pointwise fixed, which is what carries the comparison position:

```lean
-- `u` an idle position of the spliced walk at or below the comparison position's region start
-- (finding 28: `hidle`'s witness is such a position), `d` the displacement.
def insIdx (u : ℤ) (d : ℕ) : ℤ → ℤ :=
  fun v => if u < v then v else if u - (d : ℤ) < v then u else v + (d : ℤ)

def insObj (g : ℤ → LadderState Q pend) (a : ℤ) (l : ℕ) (u : ℤ) (d : ℕ) : ℤ → Q :=
  fun v => spliceObj g a l (insIdx u d v)

def insCnt (g : ℤ → LadderState Q pend) (a : ℤ) (l : ℕ) (u : ℤ) (d : ℕ) : ℤ → ℕ :=
  fun v => spliceCnt g a l (insIdx u d v)
```

`insIdx u d` maps `u + k ↦ u + k` for `k > 0`, collapses the `d + 1` positions `u - d, …, u` onto
`u`, and maps `v ↦ v + d` for `v < u - d`. So every position above `u` is fixed, the run at `u` is
extended downward by `d`, and the past below is shifted down by `d`, which grows `|s - v'|` by `d`
for a region start `s` above `u` and a region start `v'` below it — exactly the relaxation the
Phase 11.8 blocker record names as needed.

**Two things this phase must DECIDE, not assume.**

1. **Finding 29's primitive.** `hw` requires `step (insObj v) (insObj (v + 1)) = true` at every
   position, and at the `d` collapsed positions that is `step q q = true` for
   `q = spliceObj g a l u`, the inserted idle object. `IsLadderPath` constrains `step` only along
   the original walk and supplies no self-loop. The two candidates, to be decided HERE and recorded:
   (a) carry the self-loop as an explicit hypothesis on an auxiliary under an honest new name —
   permitted as an auxiliary, forbidden as a binder on any of the three recorded
   `exists_ladderPath_at_region*` signatures (Non-Goals); (b) insert a COPY of an idle-containing
   cycle instead of a repeated state, i.e. find `u ≤ u'` at or below the region start with
   `objAt g u = objAt g u'` and an idle position in `[u, u')`, from a pigeonhole over a finite
   object type. `[Fintype Q]` is available in this section (`cascadeDemand_le_cascadeBound` carries
   it), so (b) is statable here, but **no landed declaration performs that pigeonhole at this
   layer** — the one that is landed lives in `LadderPin.lean`, which is ABOVE this module in the
   import DAG and is citable in a docstring by path only, never as a proof term.
2. **Whether the reindexed countdown is the right countdown.** `insCnt` as written is
   `spliceCnt ∘ insIdx`, which is NOT automatically the countdown of `insObj`: the countdown is
   read off the walk, which is the content of `cntAt_eq_of_obj_eq`, and a reindexing that is not
   locally injective can break that. The one non-injective place is the collapsed block, where
   `insIdx` sends `d + 1` positions to `u`; there `hidle` forces the countdown to `0`, and
   `spliceCnt g a l u = 0` already holds because `u` is idle, so the reindexed form is the natural
   candidate. Confirm it or replace it with the corrected form — the corrected form is this
   phase's deliverable, not a reason to stop.

#### THE PRIMITIVE DECISION: **(a)**, the self-loop as an explicit hypothesis on an auxiliary

The decision this phase was required to make, with its reason, recorded here as well as in the
module's own subsection docstring and in the axiom test's.

`hw` asks for `step (insObj v) (insObj (v + 1)) = true` at every position, and on the collapsed
block that is `step q q = true` for `q = objAt g u`, the inserted idle object. `IsLadderPath`
constrains `step` only along the original walk and supplies no self-loop, so the obligation is
real and neither candidate is free.

**Candidate (b) was found UNAVAILABLE AT THIS LAYER, and not merely inconvenient.** It asks for a
copy of an idle-containing cycle: `u ≤ u'` at or below the region start with
`objAt g u = objAt g u'` AND an idle position in `[u, u')`, from a pigeonhole over a finite object
type. The premise that pigeonhole needs is MANY idle runs below the region start. The idle-past
regime hypothesis supplies exactly ONE idle position at or below the splice point, and
`[Fintype Q]` does not supply the rest: a finite object type bounds how many distinct states the
positions below can carry, not how many idle runs they contain. So (b) is statable here and
unprovable here, and the one landed pigeonhole of this family lives in
`FormalSystem/Metalogic/Decidability/RaySummary/LadderPin.lean`, ABOVE this module in the import
DAG — cited by path in the docstring, never as a proof term (the scoped build with
`LadderAgree.lean`'s import list unchanged at `AnchorLayer` and `CounterQuotient` is the
mechanical check that it was not).

**Candidate (a) is therefore taken**, with `hself : step (objAt g u) (objAt g u) = true` on
`insObj_step` and on NOTHING else. No binder was added to any of
`exists_ladderPath_at_region_of_idle_past`, `exists_ladderPath_at_region` or
`exists_spliced_ladderPath_of_idle_past`, all three of which remain unclaimed names in the
library (the only `exists_ladderPath_at_region*` declaration anywhere under `FormalSystem/` is
still the landed `exists_ladderPath_at_region_of_pend_past`).

**THE CONSEQUENCE, RECORDED RATHER THAN BURIED.** With (a) taken, an unconditional
`exists_ladderPath_at_region_of_idle_past` needs MORE than this plan lands: on a general object
relation the self-loop is a genuine additional premise, not a consequence of `IsLadderPath`.
Phase 11.12's existential therefore inherits it, and Phase 11.13's join inherits it through

### Phase 11.14: The `hself` Derivability Decision Probe [COMPLETED WITH EXCLUSIONS]

**THE ONE ENTERABLE PHASE OF THIS PLAN, AND IT DECIDES NO DISPOSITION.** Phases 11.12 and 11.13
closed `[BLOCKED]` with their declarations landed, sorry-free, and carrying one binder beyond their
recorded blocks. Each phase's `#### Recorded Outcome` offers the user two dispositions and routes
the choice to the user per `plan-compliance.md`'s Statement Fidelity section. **This revision does
not take that choice** — it is an unchecked Stage 0 ruling in `specs/ROADMAP.md`, and no agent may
transition it (Phase 11.15 carries it). What this phase does instead is settle the one question
underneath the choice that is a matter of fact rather than of judgement: whether `hself` is
DERIVABLE from the hypotheses the recorded block already carries, or is a genuine additional
premise. A compiled answer either repairs the drift outright or converts the ruling from a
mathematical question into a naming decision.

**This is the Phase 11.10 shape, deliberately reused.** Phase 11.10 was identified as the one
enterable piece of cascade work precisely because a decision probe needs no construction, edits
only `specs/evidence/**` and the gate script, and has complete branches. Its verdict (WITNESSED)
was reached in 1.5 hours and opened Phase 11.11. This phase is the same instrument pointed at the
binder rather than at the existential.

**Goal**: Compile a standalone wired evidence probe that settles, on an explicit finite object,
whether

```lean
hself : ∀ p : ℤ, p ≤ a → pend (objAt g p) = false → step (objAt g p) (objAt g p) = true
```

is derivable from `IsLadderPath step pend g` together with the idle-past regime hypothesis
`hidle : ∃ p : ℤ, p ≤ a ∧ pend (objAt g p) = false` (and the remaining binders of
`exists_ladderPath_at_region_of_idle_past` at `LadderAgree.lean:2227`), or is independent of them.

**The three complete branches, each a closing outcome**:
- **DERIVABLE** — the probe compiles a derivation of `hself` from those hypotheses. Then the drift
  is repairable in-library with no binder at all, Phase 11.16 takes its branch (R), and both
  recorded blocks become reachable exactly as written. The user's ruling is then moot and should be
  reported as such rather than awaited.
- **NOT DERIVABLE** — the probe compiles a counterexample: an explicit `Q`, `step`, `pend`, a
  ladder path `g`, a position `a`, and an idle `p ≤ a` at which `step (objAt g p) (objAt g p) = false`.
  Then `hself` is a genuine premise, confirmed by machine-checked object rather than by the
  in-source argument alone (`LadderAgree.lean:1758-1790`, `:2214-2226`), and the ruling is a choice
  between two honest naming conventions rather than between a correct and an incorrect statement.
- **INCONCLUSIVE** — neither compiles inside the phase. Close `[BLOCKED]` with the goal state of
  whichever attempt got furthest recorded, and name the specific clause that resisted. No branch is
  to be asserted on the strength of a sketch.

**The plan-time candidate for the NOT DERIVABLE branch, labelled as an UN-COMPILED SKETCH and not
as a result.** It is written out so the dispatch starts from a concrete object rather than from a
blank file, on the same convention the phase-11.11 handoff used for its own plan-time sketch:
`Q := Bool`; `pend := fun _ => false`; `step := fun q q' => decide (q ≠ q')`; and `g` the
two-state alternating walk. Every position is then idle, so `Count`'s idle clause pins the
countdown to `0` at every position and the `Adm` side condition of the carrier
`LadderState Q pend` is discharged there; `nxtAt` is constant, which `Drift` admits; the `step`
clause holds at every position because adjacent walk values differ; and `step q q = false` at both
states, so no position satisfies `hself`. **Nothing about this sketch is verified.** The four
`Rlad` clauses are to be checked by the compiler, not by this paragraph, and if any clause fails
the dispatch is to repair or replace the object rather than weaken the claim.

**The landed precedent that makes the sketch credible and that the dispatch must read first.**
`exists_ladderPath_pair_nxtAt_ne` (`LadderAgree.lean:2878`) takes `hs : step q q = true` as an
EXPLICIT hypothesis — the same self-loop, in this same module, landed and accepted — and its own
docstring states the fact the sketch leans on: "Whenever the object has an idle state with a
self-loop, the constant walk at it lifts to a ladder path for EVERY value of the next-deadline
register: the countdown is pinned to `0` by the idle clause of `Count`, and the register only has
to `Drift`, which a constant does." That the library takes the self-loop as a hypothesis there,
rather than deriving it, is evidence for the NOT DERIVABLE branch; it is not a proof of it, and
this phase exists to compile the difference.

requires: an executable phase cannot depend on a phase that will never complete by dispatch, so no

that reads "User rulings (no agent may transition these)". `plan-compliance.md`'s Statement
Fidelity section routes a recorded statement that may itself be wrong to the user, and forbids both

drift table in their own `#### Recorded Outcome`. One ruling resolves both.

   names stay unclaimed until `hself` is discharged, and every reference to the old names is
   updated — including one that lies outside this task's declared FILE SCOPE, named in Phase

**THE ROOM LEMMA'S INSTANTIATION, WRITTEN OUT AND COMPILED** — the verification item asked for
this to be checked by writing the instantiation out rather than by inspecting the name. The
following elaborated green under `lake env lean` (exit 0, no errors, no warnings) against the
built library:

```lean
theorem spacing_at_modulus {Q : Type} [Fintype Q] [Nonempty Q]
    (step : Q → Q → Bool) (pend : Q → Bool)
    (fwd : ∀ t x, ∃ y, RladAdm step pend t x y)
    (bwd : ∀ t x, ∃ y, RladAdm step pend (t - 1) y x)
    (lab : Q → Atom → Bool) (φ : PlusFormula) {g : ℤ → LadderState Q pend}
    (σ : WorldHistory (ladderFrameAdm step pend fwd bwd).toTaskFrame)
    (hg : IsLadderPath step pend g) (z : ℤ) (hz : pend (objAt g z) = true)
    (Tc Tn P B : ℕ) (hp : ParamsOk step pend lab φ Tc Tn P B)
    (hTc : Tc ≤ cntAt g z) :
    ∃ (u : ℤ) (d : ℕ), 0 < d ∧ d ≤ Fintype.card Q * 2 ^ (plusSubformulaClosure φ).card ∧ z ≤ u ∧
      u + ((d * (P + 1) : ℕ) : ℤ)
        ≤ z + ((Fintype.card Q * 2 ^ (plusSubformulaClosure φ).card * (P + 1) : ℕ) : ℤ) ∧
      d * (P + 1) ≤ cntAt g u ∧
      objAt g u = objAt g (u + ((d * (P + 1) : ℕ) : ℤ)) ∧
      tpOf (ladderModel step pend fwd bwd lab) φ σ u
        = tpOf (ladderModel step pend fwd bwd lab) φ σ (u + ((d * (P + 1) : ℕ) : ℤ)) := by
  refine exists_typeBlock_of_spacing step pend fwd bwd lab φ σ hg z hz z (P + 1) (le_refl z) ?_
  have hroom : Fintype.card Q * 2 ^ (plusSubformulaClosure φ).card * (P + 1) ≤ cntAt g z :=
    le_trans (budget_mul_spacing_le_Tc step pend lab φ Tc Tn P B hp) hTc
  omega
```

So `budget_mul_spacing_le_Tc` discharges `exists_typeBlock_of_spacing`'s single `hroom`
hypothesis at `s := P + 1`, from `w₀ := z`, with one `le_trans` against the caller's own
`Tc ≤ cntAt g z` and nothing else. Phase 11.20 instantiates through this route, not through
`exists_typeBlock_of_budget_le_cnt_within`. **This check is a verification artifact, not a
library declaration**: it was compiled in the scratchpad and is recorded here rather than landed,
because the phase's own prohibition on adding declarations beyond the pinned set applies and
Phase 11.20 owns the instantiation that ships.

### Phase 11.23: The Pending-State Consumer Re-Measurement, the `ramp` Delivery Verdict, and the Kill-Criterion Gate [COMPLETED]

**THIS PHASE IS THE WHOLE OF THE BOUNDED ROUND THE (P-1) RULING AUTHORISES, AND IT IS A DECISION
GATE.** The ruling buys ONE round, and this is it. The phase's deliverable is a VERDICT backed by
compiled objects — not a relation, not an induction, and not a membership proof. It is enterable:
its three gates (11.18, 11.19, 11.20) are all closed.

recorded.** The ruling's Obligation names them and this phase does not narrow either:

  reading a `⊡` bit consumes at a PENDING state: the clipped register `min n Tn`, the gap `n − c`,
  or NEITHER. **Measured at TWO points, because the Obligation says "on both sides of the level
  threshold"**: at a countdown `≥ Tc_d` for a POSITIVE `Tc_d`, and at threshold `0`. The second
  point is not optional and is not a degenerate case of the first — `Tc_D = Tc_0 = 0` is the level
  the consumer actually needs, and it is the level at which a register reading within two steps is
  plausible at all.
- **LEG 2 — the PRODUCER, on `ProbeB1.ramp`.** Decide by compilation whether the gap-shaped
  register conjunct LEG 1 names is DELIVERED by the iterated splice at copies `0` and `1` on the

  — the fixture that already kills the clipped reading. **The fixture is named, not chosen**: a

**WHY THIS ROUND IS NOT A REPEAT OF PHASE 11.20.** Phase 11.20's consumer measurement is sound and
is not re-run; it is measured at an IDLE state (`stab_alphaR_iff` carries `hidle : objAt g t =
false`, and `stab_bit_ne_of_register_ne`'s witnesses sit at position `0` where

refutations are refutations AT A STATE SHAPE THE WINDOW INTERIOR NEVER OCCUPIES. This phase
measures the shape that matters. It does not re-open, re-derive or weaken anything Phase 11.20
landed.

**THE GAP READING IS THE HYPOTHESIS, NEVER THE PREMISE.** Report 18's account of why `n − c` is
the candidate worth measuring is explicitly UNCOMPILED and the report says so. This phase DECIDES
it. A task of this phase that records it as "expected", "clear" or "immediate" in place of a
compiled object has not been done, exactly as Phase 11.20's decision rule required of its own two
sides.

**THE KILL CRITERION, WHICH IS THIS PHASE'S MOST IMPORTANT OUTPUT.** If LEG 2 REFUTES the
gap-shaped conjunct on `ramp`, **the path-level route is CLOSED**. This phase then records the
refutation with its compiled object named; **Phase 11.24 is NOT entered, Phase 11.22 is NOT
entered, Phase 11.6 is NOT entered**; and the remedy is a `/revise` onto route (P-2) —
certificate-side register bridging, under which no position-pair relation carries a register
conjunct at all. **There is NO further path-level round.** A fifth path-level register reading, a
weakened gap conjunct, a fixture chosen so the conjunct survives, or "one more" bounded round are
each a violation of the ruling that bought this one. The dispatch records the closure and stops.

promote route (B-1)'s compiled refutation into a wired evidence probe so its closure is a gated

one reason only, and the reason is stated so the ordering is not mistaken for caution: the
declaration's statement must name the clip it is about, and after 11.33 the tree knows whether that

   to the agreement itself.
2. **The thresholds are SOLUTIONS of one-step closure conditions, not choices**: `G⁺ = 2 a`,
   `G⁻ = 2 b + 2`, `T = N = 2 (a + b)`, from `G⁺(a, b) ≥ G⁺(a−1, b) + 2`,
   `G⁻(a, b) ≥ G⁻(a, b−1) + 2`, `T(a, b) ≥ N(a−1, b)`, `N(a, b) ≥ T(a, b−1)` and
   `N(a, b) − 1 ≥ G⁺(a−1, b)`. The relation is indexed by TWO budgets `(a, b)`, deliberately: a
   single budget `a + b` proves a clip of `2 (dBack + dFwd)` but hides that the two arms differ
   (`2 * dBack` against `2 * dFwd + 2`), which is exactly the asymmetry the filed `(K4)` got wrong.
3. **OWED, NOT DISCHARGED**: the thresholds `2 * (dBack + dFwd) ≤ Tc, Tn` arrive as EXPLICIT
   HYPOTHESES. That they are far below `Tcof` (at least `2 ^ card closure`) is plausible and is
   **not compiled anywhere**. The docstring says so; a phase that asserts the discharge without
   compiling it has manufactured a fact.

**THE FRAGMENT BOUNDARY IS PART OF THE DELIVERABLE.** `StepFrag` admits every connective, `⊡` and
`□` included, with `untl`/`snce` only at the guard `⊥`. **`thetaC` and `mixC` each use ONE JUMP and
are NOT covered**, so nothing landed here weakens, qualifies or bears on
`cellAt_const_of_kappa_eq_schema_refuted` or `no_fibre_equation_over_kappa`. The module docstring

### Phase 11.38: The Two Jump Clauses' Statement Layer, `⊡`-Free Level First [COMPLETED WITH EXCLUSIONS]

**ADDED BY THIS REVISION, AND IT IS THE TRUNK'S FIRST PHASE (Ruling 12).** What is owed is
`exists_linked_path` with a WHOLE-ROW correspondence in place of the window. The research round's
proof stops at exactly one place, and this phase writes that place down before anything is
attempted against it. **The round does not shrink the count move** — lengthen a region, cascade
through the cap, insert a region in a tight chain — and this phase says so in the record, so that
no later round mistakes the promoted base case for the theorem.

**THE GOAL STATE, CARRIED VERBATIM FROM THE RESEARCH ROUND AND NOT PARAPHRASED.** Dropping `γ = ⊥`
from the `untl` case of `truth_iff_of_lnk` leaves (this is `PlusTruthAt`'s clause,
`FormalSystem/.../PlusTruth.lean:89`, unfolded):

```
hl : Lnk a b g g' t
⊢ (∃ s, t < s ∧ PlusTruthAt M τ s α ∧ ∀ r, t < r → r < s → PlusTruthAt M τ r γ) ↔
  (∃ s, t < s ∧ PlusTruthAt M τ' s α ∧ ∀ r, t < r → r < s → PlusTruthAt M τ' r γ)
```

and `Lnk` constrains only positions in `[t − a, t + b]`, so a witness `s > t + b` is
unconstrained. **That is the whole gap**, and it is a gap in the LINK relation, not in the
induction.

**Goal**: A compiled statement layer, with zero debt, consisting of:

- a WHOLE-ROW correspondence relation — call it `LnkRow` — on pairs of ladder paths, replacing
  `Lnk`'s window `[t − a, t + b]` with a correspondence of the entire pending row;
- its basic compiled lemmas, every one of which is provable without touching a jump clause:
  symmetry, monotonicity in the budgets, the window restriction `LnkRow → Lnk a b` for every
  `(a, b)`, and the `⊡` clause restated against it (`exists_linked_path`'s conclusion strengthened
  from the window to the row);
- the two jump clauses' SIGNATURES, written out in the module docstring and in the round record as
  the statements Phases 11.39 and 11.40 will attempt — **as docstring text and a record, NOT as
  `sorry`-bodied declarations**, because this plan carries no debt in a library module and a
  statement layer does not need any;
- the compiled lower-bound envelope `F(a, b) ≥ max (2 a + b − 1) (2 b + 2)` recorded with its three
  witnessing families (`sigC`, `thetaC`, `mixC`) and with the arithmetic that the repaired clip
  dominates it.

**`⊡`-FREE LEVEL FIRST, AND THE ORDER IS THE RULING.** `LnkRow` is stated and its clauses attempted
at the `⊡`-free level — one history, one row — before the `⊡`-carrying level, which re-chooses the
history at every state and multiplies the correspondence obligation. Phase 11.40 performs the lift,
and only after Phase 11.39 has closed the one-history case.

Exactly one of:

**THE RELATION, FIXED AT PLAN LEVEL SO THE ROUND ATTACKS IT RATHER THAN DESIGNS IT.** `S` is
`Zrel` with ONE conjunct added, and the modulus comes from the OBJECT rather than from the formula:

```
S (P : ℕ) (a b : ℕ) (x y : LadderState Q pend) : Prop :=
  Zrel a b x y ∧ ((x : Q × ℕ × ℕ).2.1 : ℤ) ≡ ((y : Q × ℕ × ℕ).2.1 : ℤ) [ZMOD (P + 1)]
```

the second conjunct being the COUNTDOWN coordinate's residue modulo `P + 1`. **`P + 1` is not a new
parameter**: `paramsOkK1` (`CounterQuotient.lean:866`) already requires every object cycle length,
every product cycle length and `satPeriod` to divide it, so the modulus is the one `(K1)` carries
and the relation costs the parameter layer nothing. The exact Lean spelling of the congruence
(`Int.ModEq`, `ZMod`, or a `∣` of a difference) is the dispatch's to choose by what proves most
easily; **the CONTENT is fixed and a different modulus, a formula-derived modulus, or a residue on
the register instead of the countdown is a new ruling and is routed, not taken.**

**WHY THIS RELATION AND NOT ANOTHER, AS AN ARGUMENT THAT IS NOT A THEOREM.** On `C3` the pending
part is a `2`-cycle `p0 ⇄ p1`; `objAt_flip` forces the object walk inside a pending region to
alternate; and the refuting pair `xC m = (p0, 2 m, 2 m)`, `yC m = (p0, 2 m + 1, 2 m + 1)` has
countdowns of DIFFERENT PARITY, so its two regions end at `p0` and at `p1` and
`LnkRow.region_end_obj` is violated. The residue conjunct modulo `P + 1` — which `2` divides, by
`(K1)` — **excludes exactly that pair**. That is why the round is worth running. **It is an
argument from the fixture's shape and it is a theorem of no file**; the first task re-derives it
against the live fixture, and the refutation attempt then goes looking for a pair the argument does
NOT exclude, on an object whose cycle structure is richer than a single `2`-cycle.

### Phase 11.43: ROUTE (N-1) — The BRANCHING-Pending Fixture, Constructed Because It Does Not Exist [COMPLETED]

**ADDED BY THIS REVISION (Ruling 19).** Decision 19 requires the refutation attempt of Phase 11.44
to run on `R4` **and** on an object whose pending part BRANCHES, and names a relation adopted
without the second attempt as a non-discharge. **No branching-pending object exists in the evidence
tree.** `C3`'s pending part is a forced `2`-cycle, `R4`'s a forced `3`-cycle, and Phase 11.41's own
record states as a measured finding that nothing else under `specs/evidence/` was re-usable even for
`R4`. This phase builds the missing object and compiles the facts the next phase will cite; **it
states no relation and attempts no refutation**, which is the separation Ruling 19 exists to keep.

**WHY A SEPARATE PHASE RATHER THAN THE FIRST TASK OF 11.44.** A fixture built inside the dispatch
that measures it is a fixture fitted to whichever attack looked tractable — the same failure
Phase 11.20's ordering rule was written for, one route later. The fixture's shape is fixed here, at
plan level, and 11.44 attacks what it finds rather than what it would prefer.

**WHAT 11.41 LEFT LANDED AND THIS PHASE BUILDS BESIDE, NAMED SO NOTHING IS RE-PROVED.** In the wired
probe `specs/evidence/seam-gluing-ray-product/ladder-row-link-residue-obstruction.lean`: the `R4`
block — `Fintype R4` (`:352`), `stepR` (`:354`), `pendR` (`:364`), `rotR` (`:369`), `stepR_pend`
(`:375`), `three_mem_objCycleLens_R4` (`:380`), `fwdR` (`:400`), `bwdR` (`:434`), `objAt_rot`
(`:453`) — which is the template this phase follows. **A dispatch that finds itself re-proving any of
these has mis-scoped the phase.**

**Goal**: ONE compiled object with a BRANCHING pending part, `(K1)`-admissible, NON-VACUOUS, and
nothing else. The shape is fixed here so the phase constructs rather than designs:

1. **`B5`**, five states — `b0`, `b1`, `b2`, `b3` and an idle sink — with `Fintype` and
   `DecidableEq` instances, `stepB : B5 → B5 → Bool` and `pendB : B5 → Bool` marking `b0`-`b3`
   pending and the sink idle.
2. **The branch, COMPILED rather than asserted**: `stepB b0 b1 = true`, `stepB b0 b2 = true`,
   `b1 ≠ b2`, and both `b1` and `b2` pending — landed as one lemma (suggested name
   `branching_pendB`). **This is the defining property of the fixture and a phase that ships `B5`
   without it has shipped `R4` with extra states.**
3. **The two pending cycles**: `b1 → b0` closes a cycle of length `2`, and `b2 → b3 → b0` one of
   length `3`. Land BOTH memberships — `two_mem_objCycleLens_B5` and `three_mem_objCycleLens_B5` —
   in the shape `two_mem_objCycleLens_C3` and `three_mem_objCycleLens_R4` already use. **The `(K1)`
   consequence is recorded, not imposed**: an admissible `P` for this object satisfies `2 ∣ P + 1`
   AND `3 ∣ P + 1`, so `6 ∣ P + 1`; that is a constraint Phase 11.44 states in its refutation's
   hypotheses and never a new parameter condition.
4. **Seriality**: `fwdB` and `bwdB`, mirroring `fwdR` (`:400`) and `bwdR` (`:434`).
5. **NON-VACUITY, as a first-class deliverable and not a courtesy**: an explicit `gB : ℤ →
   LadderState B5 pendB` with a compiled `IsLadderPath stepB pendB gB`. **A refutation reading "no
   row-linked pair of ladder paths exists" is worth nothing on an object through which no ladder
   path exists at all**, and this plan forbids a vacuous object in the same breath as it forbids
   `sorry`.

Exactly one of:

- **outcome (a) — THE FIXTURE LANDS.** All five items compiled, `#print axioms` a subset of
  `[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]`, the evidence gate still green. Phase 11.44 is licensed.
- **outcome (b) — NO SUCH OBJECT CAN BE BUILT WITHIN THE ROUND.** If the carrier condition `Adm`,
  the ladder conditions or `(K1)`-admissibility turn out to exclude every branching pending object —
  or if the non-vacuity witness cannot be produced for the one built — **that is a ROUTE FINDING and
  it is this phase's result**, not a reason to proceed without the fixture. The phase records the
  obstruction with the clause that blocks it named, returns `[PARTIAL]`, and **a `/revise` is owed**:
  decision 19's obligation cannot be discharged as written if its second fixture cannot exist.
  Phase 11.44 is NOT entered on outcome (b) with a single-fixture attack.

#### Reasoned Exclusions

| Item | Reason | Evidence |
|------|--------|----------|
| `certBiInfK` of `Real` (condition (2)) | Quantifies `relK`, whose counter conjunct is `RK Tc Tn P B (pend x.1) (pend y.1) x.2.2 y.2.2`. No theorem of this library derives an `RK` edge from an actual `Count`/`Drift` step at arbitrary counters, so a successor-and-predecessor claim inside `Real` cannot be stated, let alone proved, from a ladder history alone. | `grep -rn "RK Tc" FormalSystem/ --include=*.lean` returns three lines, all in `CounterQuotient.lean`: the `Decidable` instance, `rk_iff`'s own statement, and `relK`'s definition. `CounterQuotient.lean`'s `R_K` section docstring: "NOTHING below says the image is faithful — that every counter step of a ladder history is an `R_K` edge at the two classes — and nothing assumes it: that is the gated counter-lift lemma's own content (obligations (2) and (3))". |
| `certFwdK` of `Real` (condition (3)) | Its `DischPathK` quantifies `relK (f i) (f (i + 1))` at every position of the discharge path, so it inherits the same missing step. The temporal content itself is available — `untl_mem_tpOf_iff` (`LadderAgree.lean`) gives the fulfilling position and the guard along the intervening stretch of the SAME history — and the discharge path would be the contiguous stretch `z, z+1, …, z+m` of that history, every position of which lies in `Real` by `mem_real_realItem`. The one missing link is the relation between consecutive positions. | Same as the row above, plus `DischPathK`'s own definition in `CounterQuotient.lean`, whose fourth conjunct is `∀ i < m, rel (f i) (f (i + 1)) ∧ f (i + 1) ∈ R`. |
| `certBwdK` of `Real` (condition (4)) | The past-directed mirror of the row above, along the reversed `relK`; `snce_mem_tpOf_iff` supplies the temporal content and the same relation link is missing. | Same as the two rows above. |

**What the three exclusions need, stated so a successor does not re-derive it.** One lemma, and
its statement is:

```lean
theorem rk_of_count_drift (Tc Tn P B : ℕ) (px py : Bool) (c n c' n' : ℕ)
    (hc : Count px py c n c') (hd : Drift n n') :
    RK Tc Tn P B px py (kappa Tc Tn P B (c, n)) (kappa Tc Tn P B (c', n'))
```

By `rk_iff` this asks for `x, y ∈ repsCnt Tc Tn P B` with `kappa x = kappa (c, n)`,
`kappa y = kappa (c', n')`, `Count px py x.1 x.2 y.1` and `Drift x.2 y.2`. Three findings about
it, each derived at this phase's close rather than guessed:

1. **It is not a reduction coordinate by coordinate.** `kappa`'s fifth coordinate
   `clipIdx B c n` COUPLES the two counters, so reducing each counter independently inside its own
   threshold and residue class can move the gap. At `c = 100`, `n = 101`, `B = 3`, `Tc = Tn = 1`,
   `P = 0` the independent reduction sends both coordinates to `3` and the gap from `1` to `0`,
   which is a different class.
2. **A COMMON downward shift by a multiple of `P + 1` does preserve all five coordinates** — that
   is `kappa_eq_of_shift` (`LadderAgree.lean`) read downward, since a common shift leaves the gap
   alone — but it is bounded by whichever counter reaches its own threshold first, so it does not
   by itself bring a pair with a large gap into range. The construction therefore needs the
   saturated-gap regime (`|n - c| ≥ B`, where the two coordinates decouple because the clip is
   pinned at `0` or `2B`) as a second case, and the `py = false` arm of `Count` as a third, where
   `c' = 0` is forced and cannot be shifted at all.
3. **Whether `repsCnt`'s own bound `Tc + Tn + P + B + 2` suffices for that construction is
   itself open**, and nothing in this phase assumes it. If it does not, `rk_of_count_drift` is
   false as stated and the bound is the defect — which would be a finding about

**This revision verified that the consumer can take the bundle, so no dispatch has to decide it.**
`certStabK` is a bare `Prop` and `certAdmK` a plain six-fold conjunction, so a theorem concluding
either may carry a universally quantified family; and the pairs `certStabK` forces the agreement

colliding pair in `Real`.** RESIDUE A of the Overview: the regime premise confines pairs to

candidate set or on the pairs quantified, and the phase must say which.** A statement that quietly
assumes the regime at pairs where `Real` violates it is unsatisfiable rather than merely
restrictive — a vacuity hazard this plan's zero-debt gate forbids. If no honest shape can be
found, the phase closes `[BLOCKED]` with the failing direction of the biconditional recorded and
the remedy a further `/revise`.

### Phase 12.6: Re-Read the Maximum-Certified-Set Finding Against the Widened `RK` [COMPLETED]

**NEW IN THIS REVISION, AND IT EXISTS BECAUSE THE WIDENING IS NOT SEMANTICALLY FREE.** It is a
DECISION GATE in the sense `plan-format.md`'s "Decision gates and contingency branches" defines,
with two branches, each complete and reportable. Its subject is the one inherited claim Phase 12.3's
widening threatens, and the point of the phase is that the claim is CHECKED rather than inherited.

**Goal**: Decide, and record with its derivation, whether `Dmax`'s growth under the widened
`repsCnt` leaves the presentation-decision record's maximum-certified-set finding standing —
specifically its SUFFICIENCY half, "every certified `R` lies inside `Real`", which is the direction
the widening threatens.

**The mechanism, derived at this revision's authoring (finding 21).** `Dmax` is literally the union
of `certAdmK`-certified sets (`CounterQuotient.lean:701-704`) and `dmax_maximal` (`:714`) says every
certified set lies inside it. Widening `repsCnt` enlarges `RK`, hence `relK`, hence WEAKENS the
three relational conditions, so strictly MORE sets are certified and `Dmax` can only grow. What
bounds that growth is the pair of conditions that are NOT preserved by enlarging the candidate set
— `certStabK` and `certBoxK`, equalities between a letter's bit and a fibre of the candidate set,
as that module's own docstring (`:100-103`) records while naming this very finding. The consequences
a later phase stands on: `dmax_subset_real` (Phase 15's corollary) and `ladderRealized`'s own
right-hand side are both statements ABOUT the grown `Dmax`.

**Tasks**:
- [x] Re-read the record at *(completed at the ARCHIVED path; the record's Finding 3 sufficiency half is NARROWER than this plan's paraphrase of it: it reads "every certified `R` **with `Real ⊆ R`** satisfies `R ⊆ Real`", not "every certified `R` lies inside `Real`". `CounterQuotient.lean`'s `Dmax` docstring and its "No ladder consequence" bullet were re-read by declaration name, not by line number)*
      `specs/archive/819_ladder_cell_presentation_design_decision/reports/01_ladder-cell-presentation-decision.md`
      — the ARCHIVED path (finding 21: the predecessor plan's `Research Inputs` cite the pre-archive
      path, which no longer resolves) — together with `CounterQuotient.lean`'s `Dmax` docstring,
      which names that finding directly.
- [x] **Decide the branch by a derivation, not by assertion** — **VERDICT: MOVED.** *Derivation: `Real`'s definition names no relation, no `RK` and no `repsCnt`, so `Real` is UNCHANGED by the widening, while `Dmax` is the union of certified sets and the widening weakens `certBiInfK`/`certFwdK`/`certBwdK` (each an existential over `relK`-related members), so `Dmax` can only grow and `Dmax ⊆ Real` is strictly harder than before. ### Phase 15.2: `Dmax ⊆ Real`, With Its Gated Input Named [COMPLETED WITH EXCLUSIONS]
**CLOSED BY EXCLUSION BY THE (Q-1) REVISION (decision 26 obligation 1). NOTHING BELOW THIS BLOCK
IS EDITED** — the Phase 12.6 derivation it records, and its two-route rejection analysis, are
accurate and are the reason this phase existed as its own phase at all.

**THIS PHASE IS THE `⊇` HALF OF THE FUSION DECISION 26 REPLACES.** `Dmax ⊆ Real` says every
member of the maximum certified set is REALIZED in the pre-given `ladderModel`. Reports 30 and 31
read both published sources and found that direction has **no counterpart**: HWZ's and GKWZ's
maximal-set statements are a CONTAINMENT for given objects (`𝔎 ⊇ S`) and a REALISATION by a model
**built from** the set (Lemma 5.24 ⇐), never a realisation claim about a model fixed in advance.
Under the adopted pair, that direction becomes Phase 21's construction half over a model that is
an OUTPUT, and `Dmax ⊆ Real` over `ladderModel` is not owed by anything.

#### Reasoned Exclusions

| Item | Reason | Evidence |
|------|--------|----------|
| `Dmax ⊆ Real` as stated, over the pre-given `ladderModel` | It is the `⊇` half of the filed fibre equation, which decision 26 replaces with the construction half over a model built from the certificate | decision 26 (USER-ANSWERED, carried verbatim); `reports/31_gkwz-ptl-s5-quasimodels.md` Q5's ingredient table, which marks exactly this ingredient **unsupported** and every other ingredient of the filed equation **supported** |
| Its joint consequence with `ladderSound` | **`ladderSound` together with `Dmax ⊆ Real` IMPLY `ladderRealized`, which is refuted.** Therefore the two cannot both hold as filed. This plan assigns the falsity to `Dmax ⊆ Real`, on the ground that the read-off is GKWZ Lemma 5.24 (⇒) while the `⊇` half over a pre-given model is the one unsourced ingredient. **The assignment is INFERRED from compiled objects and is NOT itself compiled** — Ruling 34 states it once and this is the only place it is acted on | `no_fibre_equation_over_kappa` (WIRED, `ladder-cell-agreement-refutation.lean:2217`) and `ladderModel_realizes_no_set` (**WIRED**, `ladder-cell-agreement-refutation.lean:3469`), which together refute `ladderRealized`; the implication itself is a two-line derivation stated at Ruling 34 |
| The gated input this phase named (Phase 15.1's `ladderLift` over the widened `relK`) | **NOT excluded, and NOT discarded.** `ladderLift` is realization machinery and is re-pointed as an input of Phase 21's construction half; Phase 15.1 stays `[NOT STARTED]` | Phase 15.1's own re-pointing notice, added by this revision |

**IF THE ASSIGNMENT IS FALSIFIED.** Phase 20's first task is an attack on the read-off
containment. If that attack lands a separating witness, `ladderSound` is the false one instead,
this exclusion record is wrong, and the statement question returns to the user — stated here so
that the contingency is visible from the phase it would overturn, not only from the phase that
runs it.

**THIS PHASE IS THIS REVISION'S ANSWER TO PHASE 12.6's MOVED VERDICT, AND THE ANSWER IS STATED
HERE RATHER THAN LEFT TO A DISPATCH.** Phase 12.6 was a decision gate; both its branches were
complete and reportable; the branch taken was MOVED. Its derivation: `Real` names no relation, no
`RK` and no `repsCnt`, so `Real` is UNCHANGED by the widening; `Dmax` is literally the union of
`certAdmK`-certified sets (`dmax_maximal`: every certified set lies inside it); widening `repsCnt`
enlarges `RK`, hence `relK`, hence WEAKENS `certBiInfK`, `certFwdK` and `certBwdK`, each an
existential over `relK`-related members; so strictly more sets are certified, `Dmax` can only grow,
and `Dmax ⊆ Real` is a strictly harder statement after the widening than before. The two conditions
that could have bounded the growth do not: `certStabK`'s right-hand side quantifies over `R` ITSELF
and `certBoxK`'s likewise, and neither names `cellAt`, `tpOf`, `Rlad` or any history, so neither

this phase names is therefore gated twice over — by the widening, as derived below, and by the

re-scope against the archived record's own `Real ⊆ R` form, or name the strengthened lift as an
explicit gated input — **this revision takes the second: the strengthened lift is named as a gated
input, and it is Phase 15.1's `ladderLift` read over the widened `relK`.** The reason the first
route was rejected, stated on its own merits rather than as a preference:

**WHY OUTCOME (c) IS `[PARTIAL]` AND NOT `[BLOCKED]`, SETTLED HERE RATHER THAN LEFT TO THE
DISPATCH.** `[BLOCKED]` is a member of `PHASE_STATUS_OPEN_ALT` in
`scripts/lib/phase-heading-patterns.sh`, so every phase-accounting and resume-scan consumer reads a
`[BLOCKED]` heading as OPEN and RESUMABLE and will re-select it — which is the exact failure the
2026-11-16 marker amendment recorded in this plan's Status line was written to repair, and which
cost dispatch 71 a round at Phase 11.6. `[PARTIAL]` is the honest resumable marker for a round that
spent its budget without a verdict, and a `/revise` is owed on outcome (c) either way.

**THE RELATION, FIXED AT PLAN LEVEL SO THE ROUND ATTACKS IT RATHER THAN DESIGNS IT (Ruling 18).**
`Mrel` is `Srel` with ONE conjunct added — the raised countdown clause, mirroring `Zrel`'s own shape
at `LadderStepFrag.lean:194`:

```
def Mrel (P a b : ℕ) (x y : LadderState Q pend) : Prop :=
  Srel P a b x y ∧
    (x.1.2.1 = y.1.2.1 ∨ ((P + 1) * (a + b) ≤ x.1.2.1 ∧ (P + 1) * (a + b) ≤ y.1.2.1))
```

Ruling 18 derives why this IS decision 19's relation (equal countdowns are congruent countdowns, so
the layered and standalone spellings are the same relation conjoined with the rest of `Zrel`), what
the layering buys (`Mrel.toSrel` and `Mrel.toZrel` as projections, so every consumer of the step
system's results keeps working unchanged), and what is permitted to vary (the SPELLING, never the
CONTENT). **A different modulus, a formula-derived modulus, a residue on the register instead of the
countdown, or a margin other than `P + 1` per unit of budget is a new ruling and is routed, not
taken.**

**THE ARITHMETIC THAT OPENS THE ATTACK, DERIVED AT PLAN LEVEL SO THE ROUND DOES NOT SPEND ITSELF
REDISCOVERING IT (Ruling 18).** The pair that refutes `Srel` is NOT `Mrel`-related at any
`(K1)`-admissible parameters: at budget `(a, b+1)` the raised threshold is `(P + 1) * (a + b + 1)`
while that pair's shorter countdown is exactly `2 * (a + b) + 2`, and `R4` forces `3 ∣ P + 1`, so
`3 * (s + 1) ≤ 2 * s + 2` would need `s = a + b ≤ -1`. **The landed refutation therefore does not
transfer verbatim and the attack must be re-aimed upward** — at pairs with countdowns `c` and
`c + (P + 1)` where `c ≥ (P + 1) * (a + b + 1)`, which is the regime
`records/round-25-residue-relation-verdict.md` says in its own words nothing is known about. This
paragraph is checkable arithmetic and a theorem of no file; the phase's second task confirms it
against the live fixture rather than trusting it.

**THE TWO ATTACKS AIM AT DIFFERENT CLAUSES, AND THE RECORD REPORTS THEM SEPARATELY (Ruling 19).** On
`R4` the target is `LnkRow.first_zero`: more residues to answer than the margin carries, which is
the count the raised threshold is designed to survive. On `B5` the target is
`LnkRow.region_end_obj`: a branch means the second path's walk is not determined by its countdown,
and **raising a countdown threshold does nothing about a choice of walk**. A record that merges the
two into one verdict does not discharge the obligation.

```lean
import FormalSystem.Metalogic.Decidability.RaySummary.LadderModel
import FormalSystem.Metalogic.Decidability.RaySummary.AnchorLayer

open FormalSystem.Syntax FormalSystem.Semantics FormalSystem.PlusLanguage
open FormalSystem.Metalogic.Decidability.RaySummary

namespace Probe761A

abbrev ClType (phi : PlusFormula) : Type := sorry

abbrev typeOfCl {phi : PlusFormula} : ClType phi -> Finset PlusFormula := sorry

abbrev CK (Tc Tn P B : Nat) : Type :=
  Fin (Tc + 1) × Fin (P + 1) × Fin (Tn + 1) × Fin (P + 1) × Fin (2 * B + 1)

abbrev kappa (Tc Tn P B : Nat) : Nat × Nat -> CK Tc Tn P B := sorry

abbrev ParamsOk {Q : Type} [Fintype Q] (step : Q -> Q -> Bool) (pend : Q -> Bool)
    (lab : Q -> Atom -> Bool) (phi : PlusFormula) (Tc Tn P B : Nat) : Prop := sorry

abbrev Tcof {Q : Type} [Fintype Q] (step : Q -> Q -> Bool) (pend : Q -> Bool)
    (lab : Q -> Atom -> Bool) (phi : PlusFormula) : Nat := sorry

abbrev Tnof {Q : Type} [Fintype Q] (step : Q -> Q -> Bool) (pend : Q -> Bool)
    (lab : Q -> Atom -> Bool) (phi : PlusFormula) : Nat := sorry

abbrev Pof {Q : Type} [Fintype Q] (step : Q -> Q -> Bool) (pend : Q -> Bool)
    (lab : Q -> Atom -> Bool) (phi : PlusFormula) : Nat := sorry

abbrev Bof {Q : Type} [Fintype Q] (step : Q -> Q -> Bool) (pend : Q -> Bool)
    (lab : Q -> Atom -> Bool) (phi : PlusFormula) : Nat := sorry

abbrev certAdmK {Q : Type} (step : Q -> Q -> Bool) (pend : Q -> Bool) (lab : Q -> Atom -> Bool)
    (phi : PlusFormula) (Tc Tn P B : Nat)
    (R : Set (Q × ClType phi × CK Tc Tn P B)) : Prop := sorry

abbrev certChain {Q : Type} (step : Q -> Q -> Bool) (pend : Q -> Bool) (lab : Q -> Atom -> Bool)
    (phi : PlusFormula) (Tc Tn P B : Nat)
    (xi : Int -> Q × ClType phi × CK Tc Tn P B) : Prop := sorry

abbrev Dmax {Q : Type} (step : Q -> Q -> Bool) (pend : Q -> Bool) (lab : Q -> Atom -> Bool)
    (phi : PlusFormula) (Tc Tn P B : Nat) : Set (Q × ClType phi × CK Tc Tn P B) := sorry

abbrev LadderCons {Q : Type} (step : Q -> Q -> Bool) (pend : Q -> Bool) (lab : Q -> Atom -> Bool)
    (phi : PlusFormula) (Tc Tn P B : Nat)
    (R : Set (Q × ClType phi × CK Tc Tn P B)) : Prop := sorry

theorem cellAt_const_of_kappa_eq {Q : Type} [Fintype Q] [Nonempty Q]
    (step : Q -> Q -> Bool) (pend : Q -> Bool) (lab : Q -> Atom -> Bool)
    (fwd : forall t x, exists y, RladAdm step pend t x y)
    (bwd : forall t x, exists y, RladAdm step pend (t - 1) y x)
    (phi : PlusFormula) (Tc Tn P B : Nat)
    (hp : ParamsOk step pend lab phi Tc Tn P B)
    (q : Q) (c n c' n' : Nat) (h : c ∈ Adm pend q) (h' : c' ∈ Adm pend q)
    (hk : kappa Tc Tn P B (c, n) = kappa Tc Tn P B (c', n')) (t z : Int) :
    cellAt (ladderModel step pend fwd bwd lab) phi (t, ⟨(q, c, n), h⟩) z
      = cellAt (ladderModel step pend fwd bwd lab) phi (t, ⟨(q, c', n'), h'⟩) z := sorry

theorem ladderSound {Q : Type} [Fintype Q] [Nonempty Q]
    (step : Q -> Q -> Bool) (pend : Q -> Bool) (lab : Q -> Atom -> Bool)
    (fwd : forall t x, exists y, RladAdm step pend t x y)
    (bwd : forall t x, exists y, RladAdm step pend (t - 1) y x)
    (phi : PlusFormula) (Tc Tn P B : Nat)
    (sigma : WorldHistory (ladderFrameAdm step pend fwd bwd).toTaskFrame) (z : Int)
    (q : Q) (c n : Nat) (h : c ∈ Adm pend q)
    (hs : (sigma.state z).2 = ⟨(q, c, n), h⟩) :
    exists T : ClType phi,
      typeOfCl T = tpOf (ladderModel step pend fwd bwd lab) phi sigma z ∧
      (q, T, kappa Tc Tn P B (c, n)) ∈ Dmax step pend lab phi Tc Tn P B := sorry

theorem ladderCons_localRun {Q : Type} [Fintype Q] [Nonempty Q]
    (step : Q -> Q -> Bool) (pend : Q -> Bool) (lab : Q -> Atom -> Bool)
    (fwd : forall t x, exists y, RladAdm step pend t x y)
    (bwd : forall t x, exists y, RladAdm step pend (t - 1) y x)
    (phi : PlusFormula) (Tc Tn P B : Nat)
    (R : Set (Q × ClType phi × CK Tc Tn P B))
    (hR : LadderCons step pend lab phi Tc Tn P B R)
    (sigma : WorldHistory (ladderFrameAdm step pend fwd bwd).toTaskFrame)
    (xi : Int -> Q × ClType phi × CK Tc Tn P B)
    (hproj : forall t, (xi t).1 = (sigma.state t).2.1.1 ∧
      typeOfCl (xi t).2.1 = tpOf (ladderModel step pend fwd bwd lab) phi sigma t ∧
      (xi t).2.2 = kappa Tc Tn P B ((sigma.state t).2.1.2.1, (sigma.state t).2.1.2.2)) :
    certChain step pend lab phi Tc Tn P B xi ∧ forall t, xi t ∈ R := sorry

theorem ladderLift {Q : Type} [Fintype Q] [Nonempty Q]
    (step : Q -> Q -> Bool) (pend : Q -> Bool) (lab : Q -> Atom -> Bool)
    (fwd : forall t x, exists y, RladAdm step pend t x y)
    (bwd : forall t x, exists y, RladAdm step pend (t - 1) y x)
    (phi : PlusFormula) (Tc Tn P B : Nat)
    (xi : Int -> Q × ClType phi × CK Tc Tn P B)
    (hxi : certChain step pend lab phi Tc Tn P B xi)
    (hmem : forall t, xi t ∈ Dmax step pend lab phi Tc Tn P B)
    (q : Q) (c n : Nat) (h : c ∈ Adm pend q)
    (h0 : (xi 0).1 = q) (hk : (xi 0).2.2 = kappa Tc Tn P B (c, n)) :
    exists sigma : WorldHistory (ladderFrameAdm step pend fwd bwd).toTaskFrame,
      (sigma.state 0).2 = ⟨(q, c, n), h⟩ ∧
      tpOf (ladderModel step pend fwd bwd lab) phi sigma 0 = typeOfCl (xi 0).2.1 := sorry

theorem ladderRealized {Q : Type} [Fintype Q] [Nonempty Q]
    (step : Q -> Q -> Bool) (pend : Q -> Bool) (lab : Q -> Atom -> Bool)
    (fwd : forall t x, exists y, RladAdm step pend t x y)
    (bwd : forall t x, exists y, RladAdm step pend (t - 1) y x)
    (phi : PlusFormula) (Tc Tn P B : Nat)
    (hp : ParamsOk step pend lab phi Tc Tn P B)
    (q : Q) (c n : Nat) (h : c ∈ Adm pend q) (t z : Int) :
    cellAt (ladderModel step pend fwd bwd lab) phi (t, ⟨(q, c, n), h⟩) z
      = {T | exists S : ClType phi, typeOfCl S = T ∧
          (q, S, kappa Tc Tn P B (c, n)) ∈ Dmax step pend lab phi Tc Tn P B} := sorry

theorem paramsOk_params {Q : Type} [Fintype Q] [Nonempty Q]
    (step : Q -> Q -> Bool) (pend : Q -> Bool) (lab : Q -> Atom -> Bool)
    (phi : PlusFormula) :
    ParamsOk step pend lab phi (Tcof step pend lab phi) (Tnof step pend lab phi)
      (Pof step pend lab phi) (Bof step pend lab phi) := sorry

end Probe761A
```

### The `(Q-1) PAIR` — ADDED BY THIS REVISION, SEPARATE FROM THE SIX CARRIED DECLARATIONS ABOVE

is a planning round that runs no build; the block above carries a compile record from
`plans/08_cell-agreement-construction-handoff.md`, and this sub-block has **none**. The two
signatures below are the plan-time pins decision 26 obligation 1 requires; Phases 20 and 21 each
diff their landed signature against the corresponding pin token-for-token and report any difference
as a Statement Fidelity finding rather than accepting it. A dispatch that wants these two checked
for elaboration before entering either phase compiles this sub-block standalone against the
`abbrev` context above, exactly as the six carried declarations were, and records the result.

**WHY THESE ARE NEW NAMES AND NOT A RESTATEMENT OF `ladderRealized` (Ruling 36 item 2).**
`ladderRealized` is refuted and stays unclaimed; its text above is not edited, and nothing is
landed under it. The pair is the architecture reports 30 and 31 found PUBLISHED — GKWZ §5.2,
Theorem 5.22, Lemma 5.24 (⇒ read-off, ⇐ construction); HWZ Definitions 6-12 and Theorem 14 — with
`ladderReadOff` carrying the `⊆` half and `ladderConstruct` the half whose model is an OUTPUT.
**The transfer is by SHAPE**: no theorem in either source applies to this semantics (HWZ has no
`□` and no `⊡` at all; GKWZ §13.2 is written for `L = K`), and no record may describe either half
as an instance of a published theorem.

**ONE THING THE SECOND SIGNATURE IS NOT.** `ladderConstruct`'s conclusion is literally the
specification report 32's refutation QUANTIFIES OVER (`no_keyed_cell_map`,
`no_dmax_construction_receives_ladderModel`). That is a consistency, not a contradiction: those
theorems say **`ladderModel` is not such a model**, never that no such model exists. Whether one
exists is exactly what Phase 21 is for, and nothing in this task decides it either way today.

```lean
theorem ladderReadOff {Q : Type} [Fintype Q] [Nonempty Q]
    (step : Q -> Q -> Bool) (pend : Q -> Bool) (lab : Q -> Atom -> Bool)
    (fwd : forall t x, exists y, RladAdm step pend t x y)
    (bwd : forall t x, exists y, RladAdm step pend (t - 1) y x)
    (phi : PlusFormula) (Tc Tn P B : Nat)
    (hp : ParamsOk step pend lab phi Tc Tn P B)
    (q : Q) (c n : Nat) (h : c ∈ Adm pend q) (t z : Int) :
    cellAt (ladderModel step pend fwd bwd lab) phi (t, ⟨(q, c, n), h⟩) z
      ⊆ {T | exists S : ClType phi, typeOfCl S = T ∧
          (q, S, kappa Tc Tn P B (c, n)) ∈ Dmax step pend lab phi Tc Tn P B} := sorry

theorem ladderConstruct {Q : Type} [Fintype Q] [Nonempty Q]
    (step : Q -> Q -> Bool) (pend : Q -> Bool) (lab : Q -> Atom -> Bool)
    (phi : PlusFormula) (Tc Tn P B : Nat)
    (R : Set (Q × ClType phi × CK Tc Tn P B))
    (hR : certAdmK step pend lab phi Tc Tn P B R) (hne : R.Nonempty) :
    exists (F : FrameOver intOrder) (M : TaskModel F.toTaskFrame)
      (key : F.WorldState -> Q × CK Tc Tn P B),
      (forall x, x ∈ R -> exists u : F.WorldState, key u = (x.1, x.2.2)) ∧
      (forall u : F.WorldState,
        cellAt M phi u 0
          = {T | exists S : ClType phi, typeOfCl S = T ∧
              ((key u).1, S, (key u).2) ∈ R}) := sorry
```

**READING OF THE TWO HALVES, so no dispatch has to reconstruct it.**

- `ladderReadOff` is `ladderRealized` with `=` replaced by `⊆` and nothing else changed — same
  binders, same `hp` position, same right-hand side. **That single character is the whole content
  of decision 26's split.** The mechanical check in Phase 20 is that the landed conclusion carries
  no `=` between the cell and the fibre.
- `ladderConstruct` carries `certAdmK … R` as an EXPLICIT hypothesis and is **not** stated at
  `Dmax`, because `dmax_certStabK` and `dmax_certBoxK` do not exist and the union that defines
  `Dmax` does not preserve conditions (5) and (6) (`CounterQuotient.lean:105-113`). Instantiating
  it at `Dmax` is a separate, later obligation and is named as one in Phase 21.
- Neither half carries `φ.BoxStabFree`. `presented_modelOf`
  (`FormalSystem/Metalogic/Decidability/RaySummary/Realize.lean:916`) does, and is therefore **not**
  the construction half; Phase 21's body records all four reasons.
